label: Some mathematical facts are causally relevant to physical outcomes, e.g. the primeness of 13 and…
paraphrase: Some mathematical facts are causally relevant to physical outcomes, e.g. the primeness of 13 and 17 is part of what brings about periodical cicadas' life-cycle lengths. So something without esse in re (a number or mathematical fact) does causal work.
note: Analyst causal reading of Alan Baker's cicada case ('Are there genuine mathematical explanations of physical phenomena?', Mind 114, 2005), attribution deferred: no pinned witness. Baker argues for explanatory indispensability, and most discussants read the explanation as non-causal; only the causal reading is a rival to the weak version. Definition audit: original proposition/claim wording retained; typed analyst siblings expose category-to-no-esse, explanatory-to-productive and selected-world guards without rebinding this source reading. The set-of-two anchor alone is not a universal set classification; a some-world denial is not a selected-world denial. See docs/notes/causal-concrete-rival-boundary.md.
